editions.text:
The day added up to 290 feeder visits and 424 detections across 20 species, with 18 heard, 14 seen, and 12 both. That is above the week's average of 258.1 visits and 414.9 detections, while the species count sat close to the average of 19.9. Visits were busier than four of the seven days before and quieter than three, with Oct 10, 11, and 12 the busiest.

Twelve species were recorded on all seven days, including this one, among them Eastern Phoebe, Carolina Chickadees, Tufted Titmice, Northern Cardinal, and Blue Jays. Eastern Phoebe led detections with 118, Carolina Chickadees followed with 61, and Tufted Titmice led confident visits with 111. Downy Woodpecker, Rose-breasted Grosbeak, and Northern Flicker were recorded earlier in the week but not today.

The audio source was switched many times through the day, between pi, pi-mic (movo-dom1), and c120, with changes logged in the morning and again in the evening. No species was seen for the first time at the station, and none was heard for the first time.
